symbols.name: N
symbols.def: Number of panel units.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: Number of calendar periods.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Largest post-adoption horizon in the simultaneous band.

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Predictor dimension.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: Nominal simultaneous miscoverage probability.

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: Radius of the calendar-time coefficient ball.

symbols.name: delta
symbols.def: Diameter of the coordinatewise approximation-error interval.

symbols.name: sigmaMin
symbols.def: Lower eigenvalue bound for the deduplicated untreated-outcome covariance.

symbols.name: sigmaMax
symbols.def: Upper eigenvalue bound satisfying \(\sigma_{\min}\le\sigma_{\max}\).

symbols.name: I
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,N\}\).

symbols.name: CalT
symbols.def: \(\mathcal T=\{1,\ldots,T\}\).

symbols.name: Tadopt
symbols.def: \(T_i\) is the first treated calendar period for unit \(i\).

symbols.name: J
symbols.def: \(\mathcal J=\{j\in\mathcal I:T_j<\infty,\ T_j+K\le T\}\).

symbols.name: E
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E=\{(j,h):j\in\mathcal J,\ 0\le h\le K\}\).

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: \(M=|\mathcal E|\), the number of simultaneous causal contrasts.

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: \(D_{jh}=\{i\in\mathcal I:T_i>T_j+h\}\).

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C=\{(j,T_j+h):(j,h)\in\mathcal E\}\cup\{(i,T_j+h):(j,h)\in\mathcal E,\ i\in D_{jh}\}\), with repeated cells retained once.

symbols.name: x
symbols.def: \(x_i\) is the observed, nonrandom predictor vector for unit \(i\).

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: \(\beta_t\) is the coefficient vector in the untreated conditional mean at time \(t\).

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: \(r_{it}\) is the approximation departure from the linear predictor mean at cell \((i,t)\).

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: \(m_{it}\) is the untreated conditional mean at cell \((i,t)\in\mathcal C\).

symbols.name: RQ
symbols.def: \(R_Q\) is supplied in binary rational form and has full rank.

symbols.name: SigmaQ
symbols.def: \(\Sigma_Q=R_Q^{\top}R_Q\).

symbols.name: Yzero
symbols.def: \(Y_{it}(0)\) is the potential outcome at cell \((i,t)\) under no treatment.

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: \(Q=(Y_{it}(0))_{(i,t)\in\mathcal C}\), with each unit--calendar-time cell appearing once.

symbols.name: Yone
symbols.def: \(Y_{it}(1)\) is the potential outcome at cell \((i,t)\) under treatment.

symbols.name: tau
symbols.type: finite vector of realized causal contrasts
symbols.def: \(\tau_{jh}=Y_{j,T_j+h}(1)-Y_{j,T_j+h}(0)\) for \((j,h)\in\mathcal E\).

symbols.name: Yobs
symbols.def: Observed panel outcomes indexed by unit and calendar time.

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: Label selecting horizon-specific or deepest-pool donor restrictions.

symbols.name: Fs
symbols.def: \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{nested}}=\prod_{(j,h)\in\mathcal E}\Delta(D_{jh})\) and \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{deep}}=\prod_{(j,h)\in\mathcal E}\Delta(D_{jK})\), where \(\Delta(A)=\{v\ge0:\sum_{i\in A}v_i=1,\ v_i=0\text{ for }i\notin A\}\).

symbols.name: w
symbols.def: \(w=(w_{jh,i})\) is a function only of the fixed design and model inputs, never of realized outcomes.

symbols.name: tauHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\tau_{jh}(w)=Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{j,T_j+h}-\sum_i w_{jh,i}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,T_j+h}\).

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: \(a_{jh}(w)\) has coefficient \(1\) at \((j,T_j+h)\), coefficient \(-w_{jh,i}\) at \((i,T_j+h)\) for \(i\in D_{jh}\), and zero elsewhere.

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: \(A(w)\) stacks the rows \(a_{jh}(w)^{\top}\) in a fixed ordering of \(\mathcal E\).

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: \(b_{jh}(w)=L\lVert x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\rVert_2+\delta\).

symbols.name: sd
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{sd}_{jh}(w)=\lVert R_Qa_{jh}(w)\rVert_2\).

symbols.name: zB
symbols.def: \(z_B\) is supplied with outward-rounded certificates for \(2M\{1-\Phi(z_B)\}\le\alpha\) and \(z_B<\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/(2M))+1\).

symbols.name: qalpha
symbols.def: \(q_\alpha(m)\) is determined by \(\Pr\{\max_{1\le k\le m}|G_k|\le q_\alpha(m)\}=1-\alpha\) for independent \(G_k\sim N(0,1)\).

symbols.name: cAlpha
symbols.def: \(c_\alpha=\sup_{m\ge1}\{\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/(2m))+1\}/q_\alpha(m)\).

symbols.name: ell
symbols.def: \(\ell=(\ell_{jh})_{(j,h)\in\mathcal E}\) is deterministic conditional on the fixed design and model inputs.

symbols.name: Model
symbols.def: The class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}(L,\delta,\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max})\) constructed in \texttt{def:model-class}.

symbols.name: Ws
symbols.def: \(W_s\) is constructed in \texttt{def:exact-width-frontier}.

symbols.name: Gamma
symbols.def: \(\Gamma_s\) is constructed in \texttt{def:bonferroni-socp}.

symbols.name: Alg
symbols.def: \(\mathbb A_{\mathrm{rep}}\) consists of a square-free polynomial in \(\mathbb Z[X]\), a rational isolating interval, and a root index.

symbols.name: FiniteData
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{Data}\) is the rational design, calibration, and covariance-factor record constructed in \texttt{def:finite-input}.

symbols.name: ConicData
symbols.type: pair of rational standard-form conic records
symbols.def: \((B_s,d_s,c_s,\mathcal K_s))_{s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}}\) is constructed in \texttt{def:standard-conic-encoding}.

symbols.name: Ksoc
symbols.space: finite products of nonnegative orthants, Lorentz cones, and zero cones
symbols.def: \(\mathcal K_s\) is the product cone in the standard conic record for support rule \(s\).

symbols.name: Pnested
symbols.def: \(P_{\mathrm{nested}}\) is the standard-form rational SOCP for \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}\).

symbols.name: Pdeep
symbols.def: \(P_{\mathrm{deep}}\) is the standard-form rational SOCP for \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\).

symbols.name: FminDeep
symbols.type: exact algebraically represented minimal cone face
symbols.def: \(F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}\) is the minimal face containing \(\{y:B_{\mathrm{deep}}y=d_{\mathrm{deep}},\ y\in\mathcal K_{\mathrm{deep}}\}\), represented by an exposing chain with entries in \(\mathbb A_{\mathrm{rep}}\).

symbols.name: PdeepFR
symbols.def: \(P^{\mathrm{fr}}_{\mathrm{deep}}\) is \(\min c_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}y\) subject to \(B_{\mathrm{deep}}y=d_{\mathrm{deep}}\) and \(y\in F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}\).

symbols.name: DdeepFR
symbols.def: \(D^{\mathrm{fr}}_{\mathrm{deep}}\) is \(\max d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda\) subject to \(c_{\mathrm{deep}}-B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda\in F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}^*\).

symbols.name: GapCert
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{GapCert}\) is the record constructed in \texttt{def:gap-certificate}.

symbols.name: FRHandle
symbols.def: The exact facial-reduction, real-closed-field decision, and interval-separation route in \texttt{def:strict-certificate-handle}.

symbols.name: WitnessInst
symbols.def: \(\mathsf I_*\) is constructed in \texttt{def:strict-witness-instance}.

assumptions.condition: \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{it}=Y_{it}(0)\mathbf 1\{t<T_i\}+Y_{it}(1)\mathbf 1\{t\ge T_i\}\) for every \(i\in\mathcal I\) and \(t\in\mathcal T\).

standard.name: Linear factor or predictor conditional mean

novel.justification: After outcome standardization, \(\delta\) bounds residual mean differences not absorbed by observed predictors. Held-out pretreatment cells can calibrate substantively plausible values, and the same neighborhood evaluates every donor composition.

This is an explicitly chosen finite-experiment regularity restriction, not a condition attributed to Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato. In a known-covariance experiment the extremal eigenvalues are computable before outcomes are analyzed; reporting results over a prespecified band excludes nearly deterministic and explosively noisy directions, while sensitivity over candidate values of \(\sigma_{\min}\) and \(\sigma_{\max}\) gives a direct calibration interpretation.

definitions.name: Exact deterministic linear-band width frontier
definitions.construction: For \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\), \(W_s=\inf_{w\in\mathcal F_s,\,\ell\in[0,\infty)^M}\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e\) subject to \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}}P\{ |\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e|\le\ell_e\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E\}\ge1-\alpha\), where \(w\) and \(\ell\) are functions only of the fixed design and model inputs.

definitions.name: Fixed-Bonferroni bias-plus-standard-error SOCP
definitions.construction: For \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\), solve \(\Gamma_s=\min_{w,u,v,g}g\) subject to \(w\in\mathcal F_s\), \(\lVert x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\rVert_2\le u_{jh}\), \(\lVert R_Qa_{jh}(w)\rVert_2\le v_{jh}\), and \(Lu_{jh}+\delta+z_Bv_{jh}\le g\) for every \((j,h)\in\mathcal E\).

definitions.name: Finite rational certification input
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Data}=(N,T,K,p,T_{\mathrm{adopt}},x,L,\delta,\alpha,\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max},R_Q,z_B,\mathsf{TailCert})\), where all scalar and matrix entries are binary rationals or integers, \(\mathsf{TailCert}\) consists of outward-rounded rational interval proofs of the two inequalities in the definition of \(z_B\), and the input length \(B\) is the total binary length of this record.
inputs: outward-rounded interval certificates for the Gaussian tail

definitions.name: Explicit rational standard-form SOCP encoding
definitions.construction: Introduce nonnegative slacks for every scalar inequality, split every free scalar into positive and negative parts, encode each predictor norm by \((u_{jh},x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i)\in\mathcal L_{p+1}\), and encode each noise norm by \((v_{jh},R_Qa_{jh}(w))\in\mathcal L_{|\mathcal C|+1}\). For each \(s\), the resulting record is \(P_s:\min c_s^{\top}y\) subject to \(B_sy=d_s\) and \(y\in\mathcal K_s\), with \(B_s,d_s,c_s\) rational and \(\mathcal K_s\) an explicitly ordered product of nonnegative orthants, Lorentz cones \(\mathcal L_q=\{(t,z):\lVert z\rVert_2\le t\}\), and zero cones. Its objective value is \(\Gamma_s\).

definitions.name: Facial-reduced deepest-pool primal and dual
definitions.construction: An exposing chain \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm{deep}}=F_0\supsetneq F_1\supsetneq\cdots\supsetneq F_r=F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}\) is valid when, for every \(k\), algebraic vectors \(z_k\) and \(\eta_k\) satisfy \(z_k\in F_{k-1}^*\), \(z_k=B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta_k\), \(d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta_k=0\), and \(F_k=F_{k-1}\cap z_k^\perp\). On the terminal face, \(P^{\mathrm{fr}}_{\mathrm{deep}}:\min c_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}y\) subject to \(B_{\mathrm{deep}}y=d_{\mathrm{deep}}\), \(y\in F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}\), and \(D^{\mathrm{fr}}_{\mathrm{deep}}:\max d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda\) subject to \(c_{\mathrm{deep}}-B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda\in F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}^*\). A feasible \(y^\circ\in\operatorname{ri}F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}\) with \(B_{\mathrm{deep}}y^\circ=d_{\mathrm{deep}}\) certifies that the chain reaches the minimal face and supplies relative-interior strong duality and dual attainment.

definitions.name: Finite degeneracy-safe strict-gap certificate
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{GapCert}=(F_0,\ldots,F_r,z_1,\ldots,z_r,\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r,y^\circ,y_N,\lambda_D,I_N,I_D)\), where the face chain, affine exposing multipliers, and \(y^\circ\) satisfy \texttt{def:facial-dual}, \(B_{\mathrm{nested}}y_N=d_{\mathrm{nested}}\) and \(y_N\in\mathcal K_{\mathrm{nested}}\), \(c_{\mathrm{deep}}-B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D\in F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}^*\), all nonrational entries use \(\mathbb A_{\mathrm{rep}}\), and the outward-rounded rational intervals satisfy \(c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N\in I_N\), \(d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D\in I_D\), and \(\sup I_N<\inf I_D\).
inputs: exact algebraic numbers and rational intervals

definitions.name: Exact degeneracy-safe certification handle
definitions.construction: Translate Lorentz-cone membership into rational quadratic inequalities; use real-closed-field quantifier elimination to obtain an algebraic exposing chain, a relative-interior deep primal point, a nested primal optimum, and an attained facial-reduced deep dual optimum; verify every equality and cone sign by exact algebraic arithmetic; and refine outward-rounded rational intervals until their objective enclosures separate.

definitions.name: Two-horizon staggered-adoption strict-gap instance
definitions.construction: Let \(N=4\), \(T=3\), \(K=1\), \(p=1\), \(T_1=2\), \(T_2=3\), and \(T_3=T_4=\infty\). Take \(\mathcal J=\{1\}\), \(x_i=0\) for all units, \(L=\delta=0\), \(\alpha=1/20\), and \(z_B=9/4\) with a certified Gaussian-tail enclosure. Let \(R_Q\) be diagonal, with diagonal entry \(1\) for every cell at time \(2\) and \(1/10\) for every cell at time \(3\). Then \(D_{1,0}=\{2,3,4\}\) and \(D_{1,1}=\{3,4\}\); the deep rule uses \(\{3,4\}\) at both horizons.

statements.statement: For every deterministic \(w\in\mathcal F_s\) and \(e=(j,h)\in\mathcal E\), \(\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e=a_e(w)^{\top}Q\). Conditional on the fixed inputs this error is Gaussian with mean \(a_e(w)^{\top}m\) and covariance matrix \(A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}\) across \(e\in\mathcal E\).
statements.justification: The deduplicated contrast identity turns the staggered potential-outcome problem into one finite Gaussian decision problem.
statements.gap: CattaneoFengPalombaTitiunik2025 decomposes staggered synthetic-control prediction error, but does not specialize the entire treated-unit--horizon vector to this fixed-design known-covariance contrast experiment.
statements.consumer: The identity gives \texttt{scpi} a covariance-safe indexing rule for cells reused by several horizons.

statements.statement: For every \(e=(j,h)\in\mathcal E\) and \(w\in\mathcal F_s\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}}|a_e(w)^{\top}m|=b_e(w)=L\lVert x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\rVert_2+\delta\). Each endpoint is attainable for that coordinate by a member of the model class.
statements.justification: Exact support functions prevent the upper band from hiding an assumed or loose bias bound.
statements.gap: ArmstrongKolesar2018 gives convex-class worst-case bias for scalar affine estimators; the displayed radius exploits the staggered donor simplex and cellwise misspecification class.
statements.consumer: The formula lets \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} report the marginal price of predictor imbalance and declared misspecification for each horizon.

statements.statement: For every feasible \(w\), deduplication and not-yet-treated support imply \(A(w)A(w)^{\top}\succeq I_M\). Consequently, \(A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}\succeq\sigma_{\min}I_M\) and \(\sigma_{\min}\le\operatorname{sd}_e(w)^2\le2\sigma_{\max}\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\).
statements.justification: The treated-cell identity component is the early kill test for a dimension-uniform lower Gaussian-max benchmark.
statements.gap: ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2015 allows arbitrary Gaussian covariance, but does not derive this Loewner lower bound from staggered donor eligibility and deduplicated panel cells.
statements.consumer: The result guarantees that repeated donor cells cannot make simultaneous bands spuriously collapse in \texttt{scpi}.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), \(c_\alpha<\infty\). Every certified rational multiplier \(z_B\) therefore satisfies \(z_B\le c_\alpha q_\alpha(M)\), with no dimension-dependent remainder.
statements.justification: This quantile comparison prevents the finite rational calibration required by certification from introducing a hidden multiplicity divergence.
statements.gap: ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2015 supplies Gaussian-max comparison and anti-concentration, while the uniform ratio for an outward-rounded Bonferroni multiplier is not stated there.
statements.consumer: Software can use a rationally certified multiplier while retaining a dimension-uniform efficiency comparison.

statements.statement: For either support rule \(s\), every optimizer of \texttt{def:bonferroni-socp} yields the rectangular band \(\widehat\tau_e(w)\pm[b_e(w)+z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)]\), \(e\in\mathcal E\), with finite-sample coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}\). The optimization has the rational standard-form SOCP encoding in \texttt{def:standard-conic-encoding}, and its optimal maximum half-width is \(\Gamma_s\).
statements.justification: The theorem supplies an implementable, outcome-independent weight rule with exact finite-sample honesty and auditable finite input.
statements.gap: CattaneoFengPalombaTitiunik2025 gives non-asymptotic staggered prediction intervals and conic computation, but does not choose horizon-specific weights to minimize a common honest bias-plus-standard-error envelope.
statements.consumer: The rational SOCP can be added as a width-optimal weighting option to \texttt{scpi} and \texttt{augsynth::multisynth}.

statements.statement: For \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\), the exact robust deterministic linear-band frontier and the SOCP value satisfy \[W_s\le\Gamma_s\le\left(1+c_\alpha\sqrt{2\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}}\right)W_s.\] The factor is independent of \(N\), \(T\), \(K\), \(M\), the adoption pattern, the predictors, and the donor-overlap geometry.
statements.justification: A matching upper and lower width comparison turns the conic rule from a convenient band into a decision-theoretic frontier result.
statements.gap: ArmstrongKolesar2018 treats scalar linear functionals, and CattaneoFengPalombaTitiunik2025 treats simultaneous staggered prediction without a minimax width comparison across nested simplex faces.
statements.consumer: Practitioners can use the tractable SOCP knowing that no deterministic linear synthetic-control rectangle can improve worst-coordinate width beyond the displayed fixed factor.

statements.statement: The horizon-adaptive feasible sets contain their deepest-pool counterparts, so \(W_{\mathrm{nested}}\le W_{\mathrm{deep}}\) and \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\) for every admissible fixed design.
statements.justification: This is a sanity and boundary corollary of feasible-set inclusion, included without novelty credit.
statements.gap: No literature gap is claimed for this tautological feasible-set implication; BenMichaelFellerRothstein2022 supplies only the shrinking-donor-set and common-support geometry anchor.
statements.consumer: The boundary check lets \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} verify that enabling horizon-adaptive support cannot worsen the declared honest-width objective.

statements.statement: Every valid \(\mathsf{GapCert}\) implies \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\). Exact algebraic feasibility and dual feasibility imply weak primal and dual bounds, and \(\sup I_N<\inf I_D\) makes the inequality strict even on degenerate active faces.
statements.justification: The finite record yields a safe numerical strict-improvement report without trusting floating-point objective differences or ordinary Slater conditions.
statements.gap: Generic conic solvers report toleranced KKT residuals; Pataki2013 supplies facial strong duality but not this support-comparison certificate with exact algebraic and interval verification.
statements.consumer: A solver can return a machine-checkable precision-gain flag rather than a tolerance-sensitive comparison of two objective values.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathrm{FRHandle}\), prove for every input \(\mathsf{Data}\) the equivalence \[\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{a valid finite }\mathsf{GapCert}\text{ exists}.\] The certificate verifier must use exact polynomial reduction and sign determination on \(\mathbb A_{\mathrm{rep}}\), with outward-rounded rational arithmetic used only for objective enclosures. Let \(d\) be the total number of real variables in the two standard-form programs, \(B\) the binary input length, and \(\Delta=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}-\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}>0\). Establish an exact terminating construction by real-closed-field quantifier elimination with bit complexity at most \((B+\lceil\log_2(1/\Delta)\rceil+1)^{2^{O(d)}}\); interval refinement must terminate with \(\sup I_N<\inf I_D\). The result must include nonunique optimizers, zero donor weights, redundant predictor columns, and tight or collapsed Lorentz-cone blocks.
statements.justification: Necessity plus a representation-dependent termination guarantee turns a sufficient check into a complete, reproducible frontier characterization.
statements.gap: Pataki2013 gives facial-reduced strong duals and JeyakumarKumLee2008 characterizes closed-cone Farkas duality, but neither derives an iff strict support-value certificate or a separation-sensitive exact-arithmetic bound for these synthetic-control SOCPs.
statements.consumer: The certificate lets \texttt{scpi} distinguish a genuine precision gain from solver tolerance or alternative optima on a lower-dimensional face.

statements.statement: For \(\mathsf I_*\), equal early nested weights \((1/3,1/3,1/3)\) and equal deepest-pool weights \((1/2,1/2)\) are optimal. The late contrast variance is \(3/200\), while the optimized early variances are \(4/3\) under nested support and \(3/2\) under deep support. Hence \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}=3\sqrt3/2=9/(2\sqrt3)\in[2.5980,2.5981]\) and \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}=9\sqrt6/8\in[2.7556,2.7557]\), so \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}-\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}\in[0.1575,0.1577]\). The fixed-pool comparator excludes unit \(2\) from the early contrast solely because that unit adopts at the later horizon, whereas the nested rule uses its valid untreated outcome at time \(2\).
statements.justification: A rational staggered instance demonstrates an economically interpretable, interval-certified positive SOCP gap rather than merely asserting that strictness can occur.
statements.gap: The shrinking-pool geometry in BenMichaelFellerRothstein2022 motivates the fixed support, but no claim is made that the displayed objective values are values of that paper's partially pooled estimator.
statements.consumer: The instance is a deterministic regression test for \texttt{scpi} and explains when an early not-yet-treated cohort carries precision that a common pool discards.

statements.statement: If \(D_{jh}=D_{jK}\) for every \((j,h)\in\mathcal E\), then \(W_{\mathrm{nested}}=W_{\mathrm{deep}}\) and \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\).
statements.justification: This exact reduction is a mandatory sanity check for designs without changing donor eligibility.
statements.gap: The equality is implicit in any fixed-support formulation and pins down the boundary of the new width comparison.
statements.consumer: Software regression tests can verify that enabling nested support leaves fixed-pool output unchanged when donor sets coincide.

statements.statement: When \(M=1\), \(\delta=0\), and the chosen simplex weights exactly balance predictors, the SOCP band reduces to the certified known-covariance Gaussian interval \(\widehat\tau(w)\pm z_B\operatorname{sd}(w)\). Rational multipliers can approach \(\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\) arbitrarily closely from above.
statements.justification: The scalar balanced special case must recover a certified version of the classical known-covariance Gaussian interval.
statements.gap: ArmstrongKolesar2018 contains the scalar known-variance Gaussian benchmark; this proposition checks compatibility rather than claiming novelty.
statements.consumer: The reduction supplies a transparent unit test for single-effect implementations.

sampling_model.design: Condition on fixed integer dimensions, deterministic adoption dates, rational predictors and class radii, a known rational covariance factor, and a certified rational Bonferroni multiplier.
sampling_model.units: The finite set \(\mathcal I\) contains treated, not-yet-treated, and never-treated units; repeated unit--calendar-time cells are deduplicated in \(Q\).
sampling_model.treatment: Adoption is absorbing and deterministic; \(D_{jh}=\{i:T_i>T_j+h\}\) identifies untreated donor outcomes at the relevant calendar time.
sampling_model.overlap: Every deepest donor pool \(D_{jK}\) is nonempty, which also makes every nested donor pool feasible.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no random nuisance estimation: weights and half-widths depend only on fixed design and model inputs, and correlated Gaussian-max calibration is reserved for a post-solve refinement.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_{jh}(w)=Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{j,T_j+h}-\sum_{i\in D_{jh}}w_{jh,i}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,T_j+h}\), with honest-width frontier \(W_s\) and fixed-Bonferroni SOCP value \(\Gamma_s\) for \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper uses a common deepest-horizon donor pool while identifying the underlying shrinking donor-set geometry.
The paper offers non-asymptotic staggered synthetic-control prediction intervals, conic implementations, and uniform inference across post-treatment periods.
The paper derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals for scalar linear functionals over convex regression classes under known-variance Gaussian errors.
The paper trades worst-case conditional imbalance against variance when constructing generalized optimal matching weights.
The paper constructs facial-reduced extended duals with strong duality when ordinary conic constraint qualifications fail.
The paper gives necessary and sufficient closed-cone conditions for Farkas lemmas and strong duality in second-order-cone programming.

tldr: Staggered adoption creates shrinking sets of not-yet-treated donors. Conditional on a rationally encoded fixed design, the proposal turns all treated-unit--horizon errors into one deduplicated Gaussian contrast vector, derives the exact worst-case bias radius, and chooses horizon-specific simplex weights by a rational fixed-Bonferroni SOCP. The band is finite-sample honest and lies within a dimension-uniform factor of the best deterministic linear synthetic-control rectangle. A concrete two-horizon staggered instance has an outward-rounded positive \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}-\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}\) interval, and the open theorem-level step is a finite algebraic iff certificate for strict SOCP improvement that remains complete on degenerate active faces. Feasible-set inclusion is retained only as a boundary check. Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein supply the published shrinking-pool support geometry, not a directly compared estimator.

project_justification.gap: BenMichaelFellerRothstein2022 is the published anchor for horizon-varying donor eligibility and a common deepest support; the proposal does not claim that its two \(\Gamma\) programs evaluate or dominate that paper's partially pooled estimator. CattaneoFengPalombaTitiunik2025 supplies non-asymptotic simultaneous prediction intervals and conic implementations, but does not minimize honest joint width over horizon-specific donor simplexes. Scalar convex-class efficiency theory does not supply the Gaussian-rectangle lower bound or a degeneracy-safe comparison of two nested conic feasible sets.
project_justification.niche: Known covariance with a prespecified spectral band, rational fixed inputs, and a bounded linear conditional-mean class isolate a finite-sample panel decision problem in which donor availability, worst-case bias, shared-cell covariance, multiplicity, and exact certification are visible. The target is the attainable honest-width frontier and an auditable test of when a common deepest-pool restriction is strictly costly for the SOCP objective.
project_justification.fill: The project derives a deduplicated contrast representation, an exact support-function bias radius, a finite-sample honest SOCP band, and a dimension-uniform width comparison. It gives an interval-certified staggered witness and poses a representation-complete facial-reduction certificate with explicit conic feasibility, exact algebraic verification, and a separation-dependent bit bound.

related_work: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2022, Section 2, paragraphs defining \(\mathcal D_{jk}\)) provide the shrinking-donor-set and fixed-support geometry anchor; no theorem here compares the proposed rule with their partially pooled estimator, and the weak feasible-set inclusion is only a boundary check. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik (2025, Sections 4.4 and 6 and Supplemental Appendix S.6) provide prediction-error, simultaneous-coverage, and conic-programming architecture; the frontier is informed by that machinery but changes the decision variable and loss. Armstrong and Kolesár (2018, equation (13) and Sections 3.2--3.4) provide scalar worst-case-bias plus standard-error logic over a convex Gaussian regression class; the lower comparison here concerns a rectangle of contrasts on different nested simplex faces. Kallus (2020) motivates the dual-norm bias--variance optimization analogy. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015, Theorems 2 and 3) and Anderson (1955, Theorem 1) provide Gaussian comparison and symmetric-convex-set tools for the correlation sandwich; the global spectral covariance band is instead an explicit restriction of this finite experiment with prespecified sensitivity calibration. Pataki (2013, Sections 3--4) and Jeyakumar, Kum, and Lee (2008, Theorems 3.1 and 4.1) inform the facial-reduction and closed-cone ingredients, while the exact finite certificate and bit bound remain the open contribution. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) and Cao, Lu, and Wu (2026) study different prediction and long-panel inferential regimes. Cerulli (2024) selects donor counts for prediction error, not simultaneous honest width. Wei, Park, Kalangi, and Huang (2026) use placebo-in-time bootstrap calibration in a different regime.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact robust frontier \(W_s\) and the implementable SOCP frontier \(\Gamma_s\) are distinct objects. The primal--facial-dual strict-gap certificate and the concrete strict witness concern \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\); a strict SOCP gap alone does not prove \(W_{\mathrm{nested}}<W_{\mathrm{deep}}\). Correlated Gaussian-max calibration is a post-solve refinement and is not used to define the conic certificate.
honest_scope: Finite-sample coverage, the contrast-geometry sandwich, the constant-factor frontier, and the explicit two-horizon \(\Gamma\)-gap witness are theorem-level targets. Weak nested-support dominance is only the sanity proposition \texttt{prop:nested-support-boundary} and carries no novelty claim. The complete finite certificate on degenerate faces is exposed as \texttt{oeq:degenerate-iff-certificate}. The covariance band is a prespecified regularity restriction for the known-covariance finite experiment, with sensitivity calibration over its endpoints. Unknown covariance, random donor selection, outcome-dependent weights, and a direct comparison with the Ben-Michael--Feller--Rothstein partially pooled estimator are outside this version. When donor sets coincide, the proposal reduces exactly to the fixed-pool problem; with one unbiased contrast, it reduces to a rationally certified classical known-covariance Gaussian interval.

novelty_justification: The closest donor-pool paper is used only to anchor shrinking donor eligibility and the common deepest-support geometry; no dominance claim is made against its partially pooled estimator. The closest inference paper supplies valid simultaneous conic prediction intervals without optimizing honest width across horizon-specific supports. The new objects are the exact deterministic linear-band frontier \(W_s\), a computable rational SOCP \(\Gamma_s\) within a dimension-uniform factor of it, and a finite algebraic strict-gap certificate problem that remains meaningful after facial reduction. The explicit staggered witness shows how the fixed-pool restriction discards a valid early untreated observation and yields a certified positive \(\Gamma\) gap.
